result.summary: Adds `setprunelock` and `listprunelocks` RPCs alongside a `-prunelock=<id>[:<height>]` configuration option to allow manual prune lock management. User locks prevent block files at or above the designated height from being pruned. Locks are prefixed with `user:` to prevent namespace collisions with internal locks, are held in memory only, and do not persist across restarts unless specified on startup.
result.problem: On pruned nodes, if a wallet is unloaded or an external application goes offline while the node continues running, blocks required for a subsequent rescan may be pruned, leaving the wallet unable to load without re-syncing from scratch. External applications also had no mechanism to hold blocks on disk temporarily or ensure prune protection begins before the node performs its initial startup prune.
evidence: PR description: "On pruned nodes, if a wallet is not loaded while the node is running, blocks necessary for rescanning when the wallet is loaded may be pruned. This PR allows users and external wallet software to manually manage prune locks via RPC, so they can protect blocks needed for future rescans and also clean up locks that are no longer relevant."
Revives and updates previously closed PR #19463.
result.scope_notes: Extends existing internal BlockManager prune lock mechanics to RPC and startup arguments without altering pruning heuristics themselves.
result.changed_since_previous: Extended the `-prunelock` startup argument to support an optional target height (`<id>[:<height>]`), resolving multiple occurrences of the same ID to the lowest specified height, and added a dedicated functional test verifying unloaded wallet protection.
result.card: This pull request adds the setprunelock and listprunelocks RPCs alongside a -prunelock startup argument for manual prune lock management. It prevents data loss on pruned nodes where unloading a wallet or running external wallet and indexing tools can allow blocks needed for future rescans to be pruned away. User locks are namespaced in memory to prevent collisions with internal locks, and the startup option protects against pruning races during node initialization.

risk.why: Bugs in prune lock management could allow necessary block data to be pruned permanently or cause disk usage to grow unbounded on prune-configured nodes.
